artifact: §1 — model enumeration, capability filtering and selection.

capabilityFloor.rationale: Every item is a requirement of the UNCHANGED compiler configuration, not a quality preference. The compiler is a tool-use loop; its default output request is 128,000 tokens and a model whose own ceiling is lower has the call rejected before it sees the prompt; ~8 turns of system prompt, few-shots, retrieved evidence and tool results need a large window.

transportProbe.method: one real Anthropic-SDK tool-use call per model through the gateway, mirroring the compiler terminal-action shape
transportProbe.finding: Non-Anthropic models DO serve the gateway Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint, so the candidate set is not limited to the Anthropic family.

compilerProbe.method: the REAL production compileCovenantToIR over real CONMED Article VII candidates. The toy transport probe proves reachability, not competence; this proves the model can complete the compiler prompt and evidence-retrieval workflow.

results.verdict: REJECTED — produced nothing within the wall-clock ceiling
SELECTED as Tier 1 — cheapest model that completes the protocol AND exercises the evidence-retrieval tools
REJECTED as Tier 1 — 18x the price of DeepSeek and less reliable on this workflow

tier2Rationale: Sonnet 5 rather than the nominally next-cheapest model. Haiku 4.5 is cheaper but completed only 2 of 4 probe candidates — escalating a failure to a model that fails the same way is escalation in name only. Sonnet 5 is the only model with a demonstrated track record on this exact workflow (the entire frozen Phase-3F run), and escalation volume was expected to be small because Tier 1 went 4/4 on probe.

methodologicalSubstitutions.how: production's own SEMANTIC_COMPILER_MAX_TOKENS env knob, clamped to the selected model's stated ceiling
methodologicalSubstitutions.why: A model whose ceiling is below the 128,000 default has every call rejected by the API. The frozen run's mean output was 14,403 tokens, far under either figure.

pricesAreProviderPublished: All prices read from the gateway's own /v1/models catalogue at run time, not from a hardcoded table.
